interpretation_history.interpretation: Route completion log shows manual meter-read route completion for 2026-08..09 at 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts. release_summary.summary: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and fix the cause of wrong bills (CL-01), framing it as a response-speed problem. Investigation established the root problem differently: dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200-1,260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), and of 3,025 disputed bills, 59% carry an ACTUAL (accepted) read vs 41% ESTIMATED (E-02) - meaning the majority of disputes come from bills with normal reads, pointing to a billing import/validation fault as the dominant driver rather than field-read gaps. A secondary driver was also found: field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 accounts (E-01). Tariff change and slow dispute response were ruled out as causes (E-03, E-06, E-04). The release that shipped only covers the secondary route-completion driver (work item W-WI-01: cross-referencing disputed accounts against route-completion detail, scope DA-TICKET/DA-ROUTE), completed and released with decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION. The dominant billing-import/validation fault (implicated by the 59% ACTUAL-read majority, E-02) was NOT investigated: the required pre-release verification VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED remains OPEN, and the remedy that would test it (querying the rule-change log) was never put in release scope. A second open verification, VOB-U-STAFFING-RECORD-VERIFICATION (corroborating SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage claim, E-07/CL-03), is also outside release scope. The release passed Layer-1 verification but failed a semantic check (root_cause_scope_coverage), and the problem-definition gate itself was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs). No protected actions (bill writes, route dispatch changes) were taken; those remain gated by K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.

output.summary: SH-CS requested an AI agent to auto-answer billing dispute tickets and fix the cause of wrong bills (CL-01), framing it as a response-speed problem. Investigation established the root problem differently: dispute volume roughly doubled from ~600/month to ~1,200-1,260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-05), and of 3,025 disputed bills, 59% carry an ACTUAL (accepted) read vs 41% ESTIMATED (E-02) - meaning the majority of disputes come from bills with normal reads, pointing to a billing import/validation fault as the dominant driver rather than field-read gaps. A secondary driver was also found: field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target for 9,200 accounts (E-01). Tariff change and slow dispute response were ruled out as causes (E-03, E-06, E-04). The release that shipped only covers the secondary route-completion driver (work item W-WI-01: cross-referencing disputed accounts against route-completion detail, scope DA-TICKET/DA-ROUTE), completed and released with decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION. The dominant billing-import/validation fault (implicated by the 59% ACTUAL-read majority, E-02) was NOT investigated: the required pre-release verification VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED remains OPEN, and the remedy that would test it (querying the rule-change log) was never put in release scope. A second open verification, VOB-U-STAFFING-RECORD-VERIFICATION (corroborating SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage claim, E-07/CL-03), is also outside release scope. The release passed Layer-1 verification but failed a semantic check (root_cause_scope_coverage), and the problem-definition gate itself was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as verification obligations (VOBs). No protected actions (bill writes, route dispatch changes) were taken; those remain gated by K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH.
key_points: Original request (CL-01, SH-CS) was to auto-fix disputes via an AI agent; this is a stakeholder claim/framing, not an established fact.

Root problem as established: dispute surge confirmed in magnitude and timing (E-05); 59% of disputed bills are ACTUAL-read vs 41% ESTIMATED (E-02), implicating a billing import/validation fault as the dominant cause, with route-completion shortfall (E-01, 88% vs 95% target) as a secondary driver.
Tariff change was ruled out (E-03 authoritative, corroborated by E-06 stakeholder claim); dispute response-time SLA is already met (E-04), so response-speed is not a lever for reducing volume.
Released scope only covers the secondary driver: cross_reference_disputed_accounts (DA-TICKET) and analyze_route_completion_detail (DA-ROUTE), i.e. work item W-WI-01, completed and marked DONE.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION because the dominant driver was never tested: the remedy to query the billing-config rule-change log (SR-QUERY-RULE-CHANGE-LOG) was not included in release scope, and the related verification VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED remains OPEN.
A second open verification, VOB-U-STAFFING-RECORD-VERIFICATION (corroborating SH-FIELD's uncorroborated staffing claim E-07/CL-03), is also unresolved and outside release scope.

Verify_completed (seq 199) shows Layer-1 checks passed but a semantic check (root_cause_scope_coverage) failed; the underlying problem-definition gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS with deferred items tracked as VOBs.
No protected actions were executed: write_bill_adjustment (K-BILLWRITE) and push_route_update (K-DISPATCH) both still require human authority/confirmation and were not exercised in this release.
limitations_explained: The release does not test the dominant 59% ACTUAL-read driver of disputes (E-02); the query_rule_change_log action against DA-RULES was never run because VOB-U-RULE-CHANGE-CONFIRMED is still OPEN, so H-RULE-CHANGE remains an untested candidate hypothesis.

SH-FIELD's staffing-shortage claim (E-07/CL-03) remains uncorroborated by any authoritative HR/contract record because verify_field_staffing_record is blocked by the open VOB-U-STAFFING-RECORD-VERIFICATION.

The AMI vendor-side gap hypothesis (H-AMI-DATA-GAP) was not tested in this contest; mdms-export access/health issues and a prior non-transient failure (seq 86) prevented the query_ami_read_events check, though a related unknown (U-AMI-READ-QUALITY) was separately resolved via E-12.

Dispute response-time is already within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d target, E-04), so it is confirmed not to be a usable lever for reducing dispute volume - this is a settled finding, not an open gap.

The underlying data assets DA-ROUTE, DA-TICKET and DA-BILL all have UNKNOWN completeness, and the handoffs H-FIELD-BILL and H-MDMS-BILL have UNKNOWN delivery/semantic validity, so even the completed route-completion correlation inherits unquantified uncertainty.

The problem-definition gate itself was only a CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning several items were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release, and a semantic check (root_cause_scope_coverage) explicitly failed at verification.
